tiers.1: Foundation - needed to read almost any ticket
tiers.2: Core - needed to write most features confidently
tiers.3: Advanced - how things work under the hood, or less common features

concepts.name: The big picture: from browser to database and back
concepts.summary: A page request goes browser -> security -> controller -> service -> repository -> entity -> PostgreSQL, and back as data model -> view model -> Thymeleaf template -> HTML. Each layer is a different package with one job.
concepts.why: Every ticket touches some slice of this flow; knowing the slice tells you which files to change.

concepts.name: Package layout: what lives where
concepts.summary: controllers/, services/, database/{entity,repository}/, models/{dataModels,requestModels,viewModels}/, journeys/, validation/, config/, annotations/, clients/, helpers/, constants/, exceptions/, application/ (task runners) and local/ (dev-only stubs).
concepts.why: Finding the right package is the first step of every change, and reviewers expect code in the conventional place.

concepts.name: Entities vs data, request/form and view models
concepts.summary: Entities mirror tables; data models carry domain data between services; request/form models receive user input (with validation); view models are shaped for one template. Converters and builders map between them.
concepts.why: Keeps database structure out of templates and user input away from entities, so each can change independently.

concepts.name: The journey framework (multi-step forms)
concepts.summary: Multi-page forms are journeys: a factory uses the builder DSL to wire steps (pages) and tasks into a directed graph; each step has a step config and form model; a generic controller endpoint dispatches requests to the current step.
concepts.why: Most user-facing features (registrations, updates, invitations) are journeys; new pages usually mean new steps, not new controllers.

concepts.name: Journey state: session storage, delegates and saving progress
concepts.summary: Answers are held in a JourneyState stored in the HTTP session (serialised with kotlinx.serialization), exposed as Kotlin delegated properties, and can be persisted to the database so users resume later.
concepts.why: Explains why answers survive between pages, how 'save and return later' works and why state classes look unusual.

concepts.name: One codebase, several run modes
concepts.summary: The same jar runs as the web server, as one-off scheduled tasks, or as queue workers (email, virus-scan results). Profiles plus the Prsdb* annotations decide which beans exist in each mode.
concepts.why: Explains why there are @PrsdbWebService and @PrsdbTaskService, and why a bean can be 'missing' in one mode.

concepts.name: The build: Gradle, Kotlin plugins and frontend assets
concepts.summary: build.gradle.kts applies the Kotlin, Spring Boot, ktlint and Flyway plugins, declares dependencies, and runs npm/Rollup to bundle JS and SCSS into static assets before packaging one runnable jar.
concepts.why: Explains build failures, where dependencies are added and why frontend changes need npm run build.

concepts.name: Running locally: Docker services, local profile and stubs
concepts.summary: docker-compose.local.yml provides PostgreSQL, Redis and ElasticMQ (a local SQS queue); the local profile swaps real third parties (One Login, Notify, Pay, OS Places) for stubs in local/; local-no-auth fakes login with every role.
concepts.why: Lets you run and test any journey on your machine without real credentials.

concepts.name: Feature flags in PRSDB: names, config and releases
concepts.summary: Each unreleased feature gets a flag constant in FeatureFlagNames.kt and an entry (enabled, expiry-date, optional release) under features: in every application*.yml; code checks it via @AvailableWhenFeatureEnabled, @PrsdbFlip or featureFlagManager.checkFeature. Startup validation keeps YAML and constants in sync.
concepts.why: Lets half-built features merge to main and be switched on per environment; a missed YAML entry fails startup.

concepts.name: How the tests are organised
concepts.summary: Unit tests for services and helpers, @WebMvcTest controller tests extending ControllerTest, and Playwright integration tests (page objects, Navigator) against the full app with a Testcontainers database.
concepts.why: Tells you which tests a ticket needs and where to put them.

concepts.name: Classes, primary constructors and properties
concepts.summary: class Foo(private val bar: Bar) declares a constructor and a property in one line; val is read-only, var is mutable; properties replace Java getters/setters.
concepts.why: This one-liner is exactly how Spring constructor injection looks in every PRSDB bean.

concepts.name: Null safety (?, ?:, !!, ?.let)
concepts.summary: Types are non-null unless marked with ?; ?. and ?: handle nulls safely; !! asserts non-null and throws if wrong. -Xjsr305=strict makes Spring's nullability annotations visible to Kotlin.
concepts.why: Repository finders return nullable results; handling them correctly decides between a 404 page and a crash.

concepts.name: Data classes
concepts.summary: data class generates equals, hashCode, toString and copy from the constructor properties - ideal for models that just carry values.
concepts.why: Data, form and view models are mostly data classes; entities deliberately are not.

concepts.name: object, companion object and const val
concepts.summary: object declares a singleton; a companion object holds class-level members (like Java static), e.g. ROUTE_SEGMENT constants and factory functions; const val is a compile-time constant usable in annotations.
concepts.why: Route segments, message keys and URL constants used in @GetMapping paths live in companion objects and constants/.

concepts.name: Enums, sealed classes and when
concepts.summary: enum class models fixed choices (stored as DB values, form options, step modes); sealed classes model a closed set of subtypes; when expressions over either must cover every case.
concepts.why: The compiler forces you to handle new enum values or subtypes everywhere they're switched on.

concepts.name: Lambdas, collection operations and scope functions
concepts.summary: Functions can take lambdas (trailing-lambda syntax); collections use map/filter/associate; scope functions let/apply/also/run/with configure or transform an object in a block.
concepts.why: Builder DSLs, view-model building and null handling all rely on these idioms.

concepts.name: Extension functions
concepts.summary: fun String.foo() adds a function to an existing type without subclassing it; PRSDB keeps them in helpers/extensions/.
concepts.why: Explains methods that seem to appear on library classes (e.g. MessageSource helpers).

concepts.name: Annotations in Kotlin (declaring, meta-annotations, use-site targets, ::class)
concepts.summary: annotation class declares an annotation; annotating it with Spring annotations makes a meta-annotation (how @PrsdbController works); @get:/@field: targets choose where a Kotlin annotation lands; Foo::class gives a KClass reference.
concepts.why: Almost all Spring configuration in PRSDB is expressed through annotations, many of them custom.

concepts.name: Kotlin meets Spring and JPA: open classes, no-arg and lateinit
concepts.summary: Kotlin classes are final by default but Spring proxies need to subclass them, so the kotlin-spring (all-open) plugin opens annotated classes; JPA needs a no-arg constructor, provided by the noArg plugin for @Entity; lateinit var lets entities and frameworks set fields after construction.
concepts.why: Explains why entities use lateinit/private set and why removing a plugin breaks @Transactional or Hibernate.

concepts.name: Generics, variance (in/out) and reified types
concepts.summary: Generic types take type parameters; out marks a producer, in a consumer, controlling which subtypes can be substituted; inline fun with reified T keeps the type available at runtime.
concepts.why: The journey framework's step types (AbstractStepConfig<out TEnum, TFormModel, in TState>) are heavily generic.

concepts.name: Delegated properties (by lazy, custom delegates)
concepts.summary: val x by lazy { } computes once on first access; var y by someDelegate routes get/set through another object - PRSDB journey states use delegates to read and write the session.
concepts.why: Journey state properties look like plain fields but actually read/write session data.

concepts.name: kotlinx.serialization
concepts.summary: @Serializable classes are converted to/from JSON by a compiler plugin, without reflection; PRSDB uses it for journey state and some API payloads, alongside Spring's Jackson.
concepts.why: Anything stored in journey state must be serialisable or saving the journey fails.

concepts.name: Spring Boot application and auto-configuration
concepts.summary: @SpringBootApplication starts an ApplicationContext, scans packages for components and auto-configures libraries found on the classpath (web server, JPA, Thymeleaf, security).
concepts.why: Without auto-configuration you would hand-wire the web server, database connection pool, template engine and more.

concepts.name: The IoC container, ApplicationContext and beans
concepts.summary: Spring owns object creation (Inversion of Control). Objects it creates and manages are 'beans', held in the ApplicationContext; by default there is one shared instance of each.
concepts.why: Centralising creation lets Spring wire dependencies, apply cross-cutting behaviour (transactions, security) and swap implementations per environment.

concepts.name: Dependency injection (constructor injection)
concepts.summary: A bean declares what it needs as constructor parameters; Spring finds matching beans and passes them in. PRSDB uses constructor injection only (no @Autowired fields).
concepts.why: Classes stay decoupled and easy to unit test - tests pass mocks into the constructor.

concepts.name: Stereotype annotations and the PRSDB wrappers
concepts.summary: @Component, @Service, @Controller and @Repository mark classes for component scanning. PRSDB wraps them (@PrsdbWebService, @PrsdbController, @PrsdbWebComponent, @PrsdbTaskService) to add a @Conditional run-mode guard.
concepts.why: Scanning turns annotated classes into beans automatically; the wrappers stop web-only beans loading when the app runs as a scheduled task.

concepts.name: @Configuration classes and @Bean methods
concepts.summary: A @Configuration class (PRSDB: @PrsdbWebConfiguration) contains @Bean methods whose return values become beans - used for third-party objects you cannot annotate yourself.
concepts.why: Library classes (e.g. the Notify client, RestClient) need constructing with config values; @Bean methods are where that happens.

concepts.name: Externalised configuration (application.yml, @Value, @ConfigurationProperties)
concepts.summary: Settings live in application*.yml and environment variables; beans read them with @Value("${key}") or bind a whole prefix with @ConfigurationProperties.
concepts.why: The same build runs in local, test, nft and production with different URLs, keys and flags.

concepts.name: Spring profiles
concepts.summary: Profiles (local, local-no-auth, integration, scheduled-task...) activate extra yml files and beans marked @Profile.
concepts.why: Local development swaps real third-party services for stubs in local/ without changing production code.

concepts.name: Conditional beans (@Conditional)
concepts.summary: @Conditional(SomeCondition::class) decides at startup whether a bean is created. WebServerOnly / TaskOnly power the PRSDB stereotype wrappers.
concepts.why: One codebase produces several run modes (web server, scheduled tasks, queue workers) with different beans in each.

concepts.name: Choosing between candidate beans (@Primary, @Qualifier)
concepts.summary: When several beans match an injected type, @Primary marks the default and @Qualifier("name") picks a specific one; otherwise startup fails with NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException.
concepts.why: Local stubs override real services with @Primary; multiple AWS clients are distinguished by qualifier.

concepts.name: Bean scopes (singleton, prototype, request, session)
concepts.summary: Singleton beans are shared app-wide; prototype beans are new per injection; request-scoped beans live for one HTTP request. Shorter-lived beans are injected into singletons via proxies.
concepts.why: Journey steps hold per-journey state so they are prototype; JourneyIdProvider is per request. Storing request data in a singleton field leaks it between users.

concepts.name: Bean lifecycle, BeanPostProcessor and application events
concepts.summary: Beans go through creation, injection, post-processing and destruction. BeanPostProcessors can wrap beans; ApplicationListeners react to events such as ContextRefreshedEvent.
concepts.why: PRSDB validates feature-flag annotations at startup and wraps flipped beans in proxies using these hooks.

concepts.name: Proxies and AOP (how annotations like @Transactional work)
concepts.summary: Spring wraps beans in proxies that run extra logic around method calls (transactions, security checks). Calls from a bean to its own methods skip the proxy, so annotations there are ignored.
concepts.why: Explains the self-invocation gotcha and why @Transactional/@PreAuthorize only take effect on calls coming from another bean.

concepts.name: The request lifecycle (DispatcherServlet)
concepts.summary: Each HTTP request passes through servlet filters (incl. security), the DispatcherServlet, interceptors, then the controller method; the returned view is rendered by Thymeleaf.
concepts.why: Knowing the order tells you where a behaviour belongs and where to look when a request is rejected or redirected.

concepts.name: Controllers and request mappings
concepts.summary: @PrsdbController classes map URLs to methods with @RequestMapping (class-level base path) and @GetMapping / @PostMapping.
concepts.why: This is how a URL in the browser reaches your code.

concepts.name: Binding request data (@PathVariable, @RequestParam, @ModelAttribute...)
concepts.summary: Method parameter annotations pull values from the URL path, query string, form body, cookies or request attributes and convert them to Kotlin types.
concepts.why: Avoids manual parsing of the raw request; a missing required parameter becomes a 400 automatically.

concepts.name: Model, view names and redirects
concepts.summary: Controllers add data to the Model and return a view name (template path) or "redirect:/url". Post/Redirect/Get avoids duplicate form submissions.
concepts.why: Separates what data a page needs from how it is rendered.

concepts.name: Thymeleaf templates and fragments
concepts.summary: Server-side HTML templates with th:* attributes read Model data, reuse fragments (th:replace) and resolve message keys (#{key}).
concepts.why: Every page the user sees is rendered from a template; GOV.UK components live in fragments.

concepts.name: Form binding and validation
concepts.summary: Posted form fields bind onto a form model object; validation results go into BindingResult and are shown as errors. PRSDB uses its own @IsValidPrioritised / @ValidatedBy framework instead of Bean Validation annotations.
concepts.why: Gives consistent, prioritised error messages on GOV.UK forms.

concepts.name: REST controllers and JSON
concepts.summary: @RestController (PRSDB: @PrsdbRestController) returns objects serialised to JSON by Jackson instead of rendering a view.
concepts.why: Used for API-style endpoints and the local stubs of third-party APIs.

concepts.name: Exception handling (@ControllerAdvice, @ExceptionHandler)
concepts.summary: Exceptions thrown from controllers are translated into responses by @ExceptionHandler methods in a @ControllerAdvice, or by a ResponseStatusException's status code.
concepts.why: Gives users proper 404/403/500 pages instead of stack traces, from one central place.

concepts.name: Servlet filters
concepts.summary: Filters (e.g. OncePerRequestFilter) wrap every request before Spring MVC sees it; their order matters.
concepts.why: Used for cross-cutting concerns such as CSP nonces, trailing slashes and token validation.

concepts.name: Handler interceptors and WebMvcConfigurer
concepts.summary: HandlerInterceptors run before/after controller methods and are registered for URL patterns via a WebMvcConfigurer.
concepts.why: Back links, maintenance mode, passcode and access checks apply to many pages without touching each controller.

concepts.name: HTTP session state
concepts.summary: HttpSession stores per-user data between requests (journey progress, passcode). Injecting HttpSession into a singleton gives a proxy to the current user's session.
concepts.why: Multi-step journeys need to remember earlier answers before anything is saved to the database.

concepts.name: Messages and internationalisation (MessageSource)
concepts.summary: User-facing text lives in messages/*.yml and is looked up by key via MessageSource (#{key} in templates).
concepts.why: Keeps content out of code so it can be reviewed and changed centrally (and translated).

concepts.name: Security filter chains
concepts.summary: SecurityFilterChain beans define, per URL pattern, which requests need authentication, how users log in, CSRF and headers. PRSDB has separate chains for landlords, local councils, letting agents and a default.
concepts.why: A new URL is only protected if it falls under the right chain.

concepts.name: Authentication with OAuth2 / OpenID Connect (GOV.UK One Login)
concepts.summary: Users log in via One Login using OAuth2/OIDC; Spring Security handles the redirects and creates an Authentication holding the user's identity and roles.
concepts.why: Explains login redirects, the local-no-auth mock and where user roles come from.

concepts.name: SecurityContext, Authentication and Principal
concepts.summary: The logged-in user is held in the SecurityContext for the request; controllers receive it as a Principal parameter.
concepts.why: Services use the principal's name (the One Login subject id) to load the current user's data.

concepts.name: Method security and roles (@PreAuthorize)
concepts.summary: @PreAuthorize("hasRole('LANDLORD')") - or PRSDB's @AllowIfLandlord meta-annotation - checks roles before a method runs; enabled by @EnableMethodSecurity.
concepts.why: Stops users reaching pages for roles they don't have; every controller needs it.

concepts.name: CSRF protection
concepts.summary: Spring Security rejects state-changing requests without a valid CSRF token; Thymeleaf forms add the token automatically.
concepts.why: Prevents other sites tricking a logged-in user's browser into submitting forms.

modules.name: Data access with Spring Data JPA

concepts.name: JPA entities
concepts.summary: @Entity classes map to tables; @Id/@GeneratedValue define the primary key and @Column maps fields. Hibernate (the JPA implementation) turns objects into SQL.
concepts.why: Lets code work with Kotlin objects rather than raw SQL rows.

concepts.name: Entity relationships and lazy loading
concepts.summary: @ManyToOne, @OneToMany, @OneToOne and @JoinColumn model foreign keys. Related entities may load lazily, only when first accessed inside a transaction.
concepts.why: Explains LazyInitializationException and N+1 query problems.

concepts.name: Spring Data repositories and derived queries
concepts.summary: Interfaces extending JpaRepository get CRUD methods for free; Spring generates queries from method names such as findAllByLocalCouncil_IdAndIsManagerTrue (underscore = navigate into a related entity).
concepts.why: Most data access needs no hand-written SQL or implementation class.

concepts.name: Custom queries (@Query, @Modifying)
concepts.summary: @Query supplies JPQL or native SQL when a derived name gets unwieldy; @Modifying marks updates/deletes; @Param binds named parameters.
concepts.why: Complex searches and bulk updates need explicit queries.

concepts.name: Paging and sorting (Pageable, Page)
concepts.summary: Passing a Pageable to a repository method returns a Page with the slice of results plus total counts.
concepts.why: Search and list pages show results a page at a time without loading everything.

concepts.name: Transactions (@Transactional) and the persistence context
concepts.summary: @Transactional runs a method in one database transaction: all writes commit together or roll back on a runtime exception. Managed entities changed inside it are saved automatically (dirty checking). PRSDB mostly imports jakarta.transaction.Transactional, which Spring also honours.
concepts.why: Prevents half-saved data when a multi-step write fails part way.

concepts.name: JPA auditing (created/modified dates)
concepts.summary: @EnableJpaAuditing plus @CreatedDate/@LastModifiedDate on base classes fill timestamps automatically; PRSDB entities extend AuditableEntity or ModifiableAuditableEntity.
concepts.why: Consistent audit timestamps without code in every service.

concepts.name: Mapped superclasses, inheritance and composite keys
concepts.summary: @MappedSuperclass shares columns; @Inheritance/@DiscriminatorColumn store subclasses in one table; @IdClass, @Embeddable/@EmbeddedId and @MapsId model composite or shared keys.
concepts.why: Needed to read the less common entity mappings in the schema.

concepts.name: Database migrations with Flyway
concepts.summary: Spring Boot runs Flyway on startup, applying versioned SQL files in db/migrations in order; the schema is never generated from entities.
concepts.why: Entity changes need a matching migration or the app fails schema validation.

concepts.name: Calling external APIs (RestClient)
concepts.summary: RestClient beans configured with base URLs and headers make HTTP calls to third-party APIs; responses deserialise into Kotlin classes.
concepts.why: EPC Register, GOV.UK Pay and Plausible integrations use this pattern, with local stubs for development.

concepts.name: Message queues with Spring Cloud AWS (@SqsListener)
concepts.summary: @SqsListener methods are invoked by a listener container when a message arrives on an SQS queue.
concepts.why: Emails and virus-scan results are processed asynchronously by worker run modes.

concepts.name: Non-web run modes and ApplicationRunner
concepts.summary: ApplicationRunner beans run once after startup. With the web server deactivated and the scheduled-task profile, PRSDB starts, runs a task and exits.
concepts.why: Scheduled jobs (reminders, clean-ups) reuse services without running a web server.

concepts.name: How feature flags hook into Spring
concepts.summary: FF4J flags toggle endpoints via a custom RequestCondition (@AvailableWhenFeatureEnabled) and swap bean implementations via proxy (@PrsdbFlip).
concepts.why: Lets unreleased features ship to production switched off.

concepts.name: Unit testing beans without Spring
concepts.summary: Because dependencies arrive through the constructor, a service can be tested by constructing it with Mockito mocks - no Spring context needed.
concepts.why: Fast, focused tests of business logic.

concepts.name: Controller slice tests (@WebMvcTest, MockMvc)
concepts.summary: @WebMvcTest starts only the web layer for one controller; MockMvc sends fake requests and asserts status, view and model. PRSDB's ControllerTest base adds security config.
concepts.why: Tests URL mapping, security and validation without a database.

concepts.name: Replacing beans in tests (@MockitoBean, @MockitoSpyBean)
concepts.summary: @MockitoBean replaces a bean in the test ApplicationContext with a mock; @MockitoSpyBean wraps the real bean.
concepts.why: Slice tests need stand-ins for services outside the slice.

concepts.name: Full-context tests (@SpringBootTest) and context caching
concepts.summary: @SpringBootTest starts the whole application (integration tests use a random port plus Playwright); @ActiveProfiles and @Import adjust it. Spring caches contexts between tests with identical configuration.
concepts.why: Different mock/profile combinations create new contexts and slow the suite.

concepts.name: Testcontainers and @ServiceConnection
concepts.summary: Tests start real PostgreSQL (and other services) in Docker; @ServiceConnection points Spring Boot's auto-configuration at them.
concepts.why: Integration tests hit a real database identical to production.
